$schema_note: AUTHORED, not derived. tools/inferred_occupancy.py spends it: every row becomes the `occupants` block of the roof it names, through the generator that owns that roof, so the card says what the building is FOR when no household holds it. Add a row only with the reasoning that bounds it; never a person's name and never a household id.
not_a_reading: No page of any source was opened for this file. Each row states the USE of an anonymous roof the 668-roof programme already raised and no household's seat reaches, so that the order book's `every_structure_occupied_or_its_use_stated` can be answered for it on the card rather than left blank.
the_rule: A roof is given a stated use here only when (a) no seat in data/reconstruction/1835_platted_seats.json or 1835_off_plat_seats.json and no other occupancy programme names it, (b) no clause of the placement policy can seat a household on it where it stands — its family is not a dwelling, or the only clause admitting it asks for ground it does not stand on — so a deal declining it loses nobody a roof, and (c) the use is bounded by something committed — the recipe's own `yard_group`, or the family's line in data/reconstruction/1835_family_archetype_crosswalk.json. A stated use names nobody: it is the building's purpose, reconstructed, and it retires the moment a deal or a source seats a keeper (tools/inferred_occupancy.py refuses a roof claimed twice).

rows.value: No household of its own — a heavy timber work shed on the Randolph road, where frames were cut for the West Division's new houses
rows.bounded_by: The W5 line of the family crosswalk: heavy timber and rough boards, an open work bay and timber piles. Of the line's three uses — sawmill, boat repair, riverside shop — the first two need the river and this roof stands on blk_west_randolph_des_plaines, three streets back from the South Branch, so the use stated is the third read as a framing shop: the kind of work the dwellings of the cluster it stands in would have called on. No keeper is named: none of the households the deals seat in this cluster or the next (recon_1835_west_026 to 045) has a trade on its card for 1835, and this file names nobody. The platted deal OFFERED this roof and nobody could take it: the only clause admitting W5, heavy_and_noxious_trades, seats on `ground:branch`, which no platted lot draws, and the two heads that clause holds are South and North Division. With the use stated the deal holds it back instead (roofs_held_back), which changes no seat.

rows.value: No household of its own — the stable of the frame cottage beside it on the Jefferson face
rows.bounded_by: The West recipe's own `yard_group`: placement west_rec_037 is drawn in the yard of west_rec_033, the D5 deep-plan frame cottage the platted deal seats on blk_west_lake_des_plaines#08. A stable keeps that house's horse and cow; nobody sleeps in it.

rows.value: No household of its own — the stable of the two-storey frame house beside it on the westward wagon approach
rows.bounded_by: The West recipe's own `yard_group`: placement west_rec_047 is drawn in the yard of west_rec_046. That roof was the cluster's F1 freight shed until T-1827 carried out T-1445's verdict on it (F1 24×44 → H2 24×36 ft), and the platted deal now adopts it under its merchant_and_professional_dwellings clause on blk_west_randolph_des_plaines#01, so it stands as a merchant's two-storey house and not a shed or a boarding house. A stable keeps that house's horse and carriage on the wagon road west; nobody sleeps in it.
